input.quote: A. Capability of Computer Systems and Software. M&I's computer systems (hardware and software) are capable of performing the Services in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 16.1 gives only a capability warranty (16.1.A) and a warranty that reports are in substantial conformity with the User Manuals (16.1.B). A report/output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation conformance warranty, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy exists anywhere (Article 12 offers only default/termination remedies; the sole refund mechanic, Section 10.4, concerns Developed Software resale, not warranty breach). The blanket disclaimer in 16.1.F removes all implied conformance warranties, so the Agreement fails the fallback on software conformance and remedies. Section 9.1 imposes a term-long Services performance obligation, which satisfies the fallback 30-day Services warranty duration (short of the preferred "professional and workmanlike" formulation, which we note but do not press). We therefore add the shortest fallback-level subsection G; it is automatically carved out of the 16.1.F disclaimer, which applies "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1".

mappings.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
mappings.quote: M&I agrees to perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards and, where there are no Performance Standards, in a commercially reasonable manner

mappings.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.

ops.text: G. Software Conformance; Remedy. M&I warrants that, for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the software used to provide the Services will conform in all material respects to its documentation. For breach of this warranty, M&I shall repair or replace the non-conforming software or refund the fees paid for the affected Services.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a ninety-day conformance warranty for the software used to provide the Services, together with a repair, replacement or refund remedy, because Section 16.1 currently warrants only system capability and report conformity with no remedy. This sits at our fallback position; the existing Section 9.1 performance obligation covers the Services warranty.
proposal.summary: Add a 90-day software-to-documentation conformance warranty with repair, replacement or refund remedy in Section 16.1
